games.title: Tense Time Machine
games.skillName: Present and past tense, including the progressive form
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to learn how to use: the present and past tenses correctly and consistently including the progressive form
games.instruction: Read the sentence, then tap the verb that fits.
games.hint: Not quite. Look for words that tell you when it happens, then try again.

questions.ask: Yesterday, I ___ to the shop.
Right now, Sam ___ a book.
Last night, we ___ when the phone rang.
Is 'she is drumming' in the past or the present?
What is the past tense of 'run'?
What is the past tense of 'jump'?
Which is the past progressive of 'shout'?
Which verb is in the present tense?
Look! The baby ___ at us right now.
The dog ___ at the cat all day yesterday.

games.title: Noun Phrase Builder
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to learn how to use: expanded noun phrases to describe and specify [for example, the blue butterfly]
games.instruction: Read it, then tap the right answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Find the noun first, then the words that describe it.

questions.ask: Which is an expanded noun phrase?
Which word fits best? 'the ___ dragon'
Which word is the noun in 'the tall green tree'?
Which word describes the noun in 'a fluffy cat'?
Which phrase tells us the most about the dog?
Which word could expand 'the ___ cake'?
Which is NOT a noun phrase?
Which noun phrase is the most descriptive?
In 'the man in the moon', which part adds detail about the man?
Which word fits? 'I saw a ___ rainbow.'

games.title: Whose Is It?
games.skillName: The possessive apostrophe for one owner
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to spell by: learning the possessive apostrophe (singular) [for example, the girl's book]
games.instruction: Read it, then tap the right answer.
games.hint: Not quite. One owner gets an apostrophe before the s, so try again.

questions.ask: How do we write 'the book that belongs to the girl'?
Pick the right one: the ball belonging to Sam.
The dog has a bone. Whose bone is it?
One cat has a tail. Which is right?
Mum has a car. Which is right?
In 'Ben's hat', what does the 's show?
The teacher has a pen. Which is right?
Which sentence uses the apostrophe correctly?
The baby has a toy. Whose toy is it?
The king has a crown. Which is right?

games.title: Spelling Sound Safari
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to spell by: learning new ways of spelling phonemes for which one or more spellings are already known, and learn some words with each spelling, including a few common homophones; apply spelling rules and guidance, as listed in English Appendix 1
games.instruction: Read the clue, then tap the right spelling.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about how that sound is often spelt, then try again.

questions.ask: Pick the right spelling: when tears fall, you ___.
Pick the right spelling: a round thing you kick or throw.
Pick the right spelling: another word for mum.
Pick the right spelling: an animal that swings in trees.
Pick the right spelling: 'I ___ to go to the park.'
Pick the right spelling: to press something flat.
Pick the right spelling: 'Say the magic ___!'
Pick the right spelling: not cold, but ___.
Pick the right spelling: a pirate's chest of gold.
Pick the right spelling: a place where trains stop.

games.title: Tricky Word Trail
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to spell by: learning to spell common exception words
games.instruction: Read the sentence, then tap the right spelling.
games.hint: Not quite. These words break the rules, so picture them carefully and try again.

questions.ask: Pick the right spelling: 'I ___ like a drink, please.'
Pick the right spelling: '___ is at the door?'
Pick the right spelling: 'I ___ swim when I was five.'
Pick the right spelling: 'You ___ wear a coat today.'
Pick the right spelling: 'Are you ___ it is right?'
Pick the right spelling: 'Are there ___ sweets left?'
Pick the right spelling: 'My ___ came to see the school play.'
Pick the right spelling: 'We open presents on ___ Day.'
Pick the right spelling: 'I have ___ one apple left.'
Pick the right spelling: 'We went to the park ___ lunch.'

games.title: Proofreading Parrot
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to make simple additions, revisions and corrections to their own writing by: re-reading to check that their writing makes sense and that verbs to indicate time are used correctly and consistently, including verbs in the continuous form; proof-reading to check for errors in spelling, grammar and punctuation [for example, ends of sentences punctuated correctly]
games.instruction: Read them all, then tap the one with no mistakes.
games.hint: Not quite. Check the capital letter, the end mark and the verbs, then try again.

questions.ask: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
Which question ends correctly?
Which sentence keeps to one tense?
Which sentence uses the past tense all the way through?
Which sentence is correct?
Pick the correctly written sentence.
Which sentence keeps the same tense?
Pick the correctly punctuated list.
Pick the best ending: 'Yesterday we ___'
Which exclamation is written correctly?

games.title: Story Word Lantern
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to develop pleasure in reading, motivation to read, vocabulary and understanding by: recognising simple recurring literary language in stories and poetry; discussing and clarifying the meanings of words, linking new meanings to known vocabulary
games.instruction: Read it, then tap the right answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about the stories and poems you know, then try again.

questions.ask: 'Once upon a time' tells you the story is set ___.
Why do poets often repeat words, like 'twinkle, twinkle'?
In fairy tales, how many wishes are often granted?
'Mirror, mirror, on the wall.' Which story is this from?
'Rapunzel, Rapunzel, let down your ___!'

What does 'enormous' mean in 'an enormous turnip'?

'He gobbled his food.' What does 'gobbled' mean?
'And they all lived happily ever after' comes at the ___ of a tale.
